subject: Business Models
title: Nokia: Software Blindness
description: A short lesson to help you apply Nokia: Software Blindness.

hook.text: Nokia sold 40% of all mobile phones in 2007. By 2013, it sold its phone business to Microsoft for scrap.

buildup.text: Nokia made the world's most durable, reliable phones. Its hardware engineering was unmatched globally.

discovery.text: Nokia saw the iPhone as a worse phone: fragile, short battery, no keyboard. It missed that software was the new game.

twist.text: Nokia's CEO said: 'We didn't do anything wrong, but somehow we lost.' They judged hardware; the market judged apps.

climax.text: Nokia proved that being the best at the old game doesn't matter when the game itself changes.

punchline.text: 'We did nothing wrong.' The game changed while Nokia perfected the old one.

quiz.question: What did Nokia fail to recognize about the smartphone shift?
options: That software and apps mattered more than hardware quality
